title: SYSK Selects: How Porta-Potties Work
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the December 2016 episode on how porta potties work. Josh and Chuck cover the Taste of Chicago porta potty servicing example, the history from World War Two shipyard and aircraft toilets (the Elson chemical toilet) through the fiberglass "strong box" and polyethylene units, ventilation improvements, roll-around and honey wagon restroom trailers, the blue dye, fragrances and enzyme/microbe additives that replaced formaldehyde, the difficulties of frozen waste and servicing, and the worst-case tip-over scenario. The episode closes with listener mail correcting the pronunciation of John Cleese's surname and acknowledging Carol Cleveland's omission from an earlier Monty Python episode.
topics: enzymes and microbes in portable toilets

segments.title: Opening and Taste of Chicago servicing
segments.summary: Josh introduces the rerun and the topic, then discusses how porta potties were serviced for the Taste of Chicago, including the number of units and nightly cleaning by Service Sanitation, Inc., and how the servicing process works.

segments.title: Porta potty history: WWII origins and the Elson toilet
segments.summary: The hosts trace the origins of portable toilets to World War Two, with shipyard workers at Long Beach and bomber crews needing toilets. They describe the Andy Gump style units and the Elson chemical toilet, and read pilot accounts of its problems.

segments.title: Chemical toilets versus outhouses
segments.summary: Josh explains that a chemical toilet is any toilet using a substance to break down waste, and distinguishes porta potties as self-contained units from outhouses dug over holes in the ground, noting public health benefits and water savings.

segments.title: Strong box, polyethylene, ventilation and mobile units
segments.summary: The hosts cover the fiberglass strong box by Harvey Heather, its drawbacks, the shift to polyethylene units by George Harding's company, Harding's ventilation design and translucent roof, and roll-around and crane-lifted toilets. They also cover honey wagon restroom trailers, including the 1984 Columbus, Ohio origin.

segments.title: Inside a porta potty: blue dye, fragrance and additives
segments.summary: The hosts explain the blue dye used to mask feces, fragrance additives, and the shift away from formaldehyde toward enzymes and microbes that break down waste and odor, including effects of heat on odor and treatment.
topics: enzymes and microbes in portable toilets

segments.title: Servicing challenges, frozen waste and tip-over disasters
segments.summary: The hosts discuss servicing units: adding fresh water and solution, objects found in tanks, frozen waste and use of brine and rock salt, and the worst case of a unit tipping onto its door.

segments.title: Closing thoughts and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts thank service workers, mention the Police Academy film reference, and read listener mail correcting the pronunciation of John Cleese's surname and noting Carol Cleveland's omission from an earlier Monty Python episode.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener mail about John Cleese's surname and Carol Cleveland, followed by contact information and the sign-off.
